extraction_notes: The 25 degC forward-voltage, reverse-leakage, and capacitance traces were digitized from the supplied PDF figures; digitized values are approximate typical readings, not tabulated limits.
Figure 2 forward current values were read on the logarithmic 0.01 to 100 mA axis and converted from mA to A; forward voltage axis is linear from 0.1 to 1.0 V.
Figure 3 reverse current values were read on the logarithmic 0.001 to 10 mA axis and converted from mA to A; reverse voltage axis is linear from 0 to 70 V.
Figure 4 capacitance values were read on the linear 0.48 to 0.60 pF axis and converted from pF to F; the figure is paired with the table test frequency of 1.0 MHz.

The electrical-characteristics table gives maximum forward voltage at four currents, maximum reverse leakage, maximum capacitance, maximum reverse-recovery time, and minimum reverse breakdown voltage at the conditions recorded above.
The 60 microampere reverse-leakage limit at VR = 25 V and TJ = 150 degC was not used as the nominal reverse-current input because it is a separate high-temperature row.
Maximum ratings include VR = 100 V and IF = 200 mA for each diode; these ratings define operating limits and were not treated as typical curve points.
omission_reason: No temperature sweep or reverse-recovery waveform was digitized; the extraction uses the minimum 25 degC curve set plus the tabulated electrical limits needed for a signal-diode F2 attempt.
